MentalMixer.notes: The maker named none of the 52 inputs, so the lines come from the code and from the row labels printed down the right of the panel: In, Vol, Vol CV, Pan, Pan CV, Aux 1, Aux 2 and Mute, with Aux 1, Aux 2, Master Volume and Main Outs across the top. The channel level CV is applied twice to the aux sends: src/MentalMixer.cpp:150-151 multiplies the already-scaled channel by the same clamped CV again, so a send follows the square of that CV while the stereo mix follows it once. The mute states start true, meaning passing, and the button toggles; the light is written from the state and then cleared again when the channel is stopped (src/MentalMixer.cpp:136 and 147). The master mix knob has no CV input. Panning is a linear crossfade doubled, as in SubMixer, so a centred channel reaches each side at its knob level and a hard-panned one at twice that.

The lower bank's jacks are read through the upper bank's trigger objects: src/MentalRadioButtons.cpp:120 calls button_triggers[i].process on the INS2 voltage where button2_triggers[i] was plainly meant, so a gate patched to a lower-bank jack shares its trigger state with the upper-bank button and jack at the same number and the two interfere. In every case here a button and a jack are fed to one trigger inside a single || expression, which hands the trigger two different values per sample and makes a steady high voltage re-fire on every sample; that is why the lines say a gate holds the selection rather than firing once.
